MeToo Revolution – Consent No Longer Exists

LONDON - England - Consent no longer exists when any historical event can be presented to a court of law without any evidence, anonymously, and with word alone to convict a man.

By Delicta maiorum immeritus lues
November 11, 2026
Facebook
Twitter
Pinterest

    The recent court case regarding a certain celebrity has revealed a big shift in the concept of “consent” regarding sexual relations. Consent no longer exists in 2026. Not to denigrate the victims of the convicted rapist Russell Brand, but to highlight a new precedent in the feminist MeToo movement that activated many of these trials. Yes, women are abused and raped without their consent, and yes, some are left with conflicting feelings and do not report the terrible event immediately, but inversely, it has to be recognised that there are some women who utilise protected anonymity and consent as a weapon to do particular harm to their mark.

    According to the new MeToo Law

    A man can be accused by any woman of rape after as many years have passed. She does not have to contribute any form of evidence apart from her word to have a man convicted and sentenced to prison. If after consensual sex occurred, and she changes her mind, or she feels spiteful that the man is now a successful celebrity, or whatever, she can file a rape case. She can claim to be raped despite continuing sexual relations with a man after the so-called rape occurred.

    The clincher here is that no evidence is needed to commit a man to prison. It is her words only that matter in a court of law.

    In this respect, consent no longer exists because any historical event dating back decades can be altered, changed and presented to a court of law by a woman purely with her words, anonymously, with no physical or recorded evidence required to convict a man. Unlike prudent law in the United States, in the UK there is no statute of limitations.

    Trial and conviction via social media

    For a man to have sexual relations with any woman now and not go to prison, she must not be aggravated by the man in any way, in the present and future. If she is aggravated, either the man has a differing political view in the future, or he says or does something she does not agree with, then she can change her mind about the prior consent. Celebrities and influential men, or high-ranking businessmen or politicians, are at the highest risk from the disappearance of consent and are most vulnerable to trial by social media. The motivation of their accusers can range from monetary gain to the simple malicious destruction of their mark’s character and reputation. Men are thus at the mercy of any woman’s mood or mindset, in the present, in the past, and in the future.

    Consent is dead. MeToo killed consent. Consent no longer exists in a world where the truth and justice does not exist any more.

    Women won, and they won totally.
